raw.assessment: Preassembly plausibly lets workers check the selected configuration before dispatch while retaining removable partitions. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, so this workflow sometimes approaches the time target; its 11-minute overall median and customer difficulties do not establish success. Mixed batches contain every extreme delay, but layout complexity could explain that association. A concrete limit on a width-only insertion explanation is D2-O5: widths overlap between first-attempt and retried parts. This weakens width alone as a sufficient discriminator without excluding fit problems. Missing-part reports are not independently verified physical omissions in all five cases. All causal accounts below remain hypotheses within this synthetic case.

openings.claim: Switching configurations may increase selection and checking time even when the parts and insertion method remain unchanged.
openings.delta: Separates a configuration-switch cost from intrinsic layout complexity and insertion difficulty.
openings.prediction: For matched layouts and workers, interleaved orders take longer specifically during selection or checking than repeated-layout blocks; a complexity-only account predicts no comparable switching difference.
openings.probe: Use 12 spare-board samples as six matched pairs across the three layouts and two workers. Counterbalance block/interleaved sequence and record selection, insertion, checking and packing separately; independently count required components. Treat the small comparison as directional evidence.
assumptions: The comparison fits available working time without delaying the fixed delivery date.

openings.claim: The generic three-layout diagram may leave the role of a present, correct short partition ambiguous.
openings.delta: Tests instruction ambiguity separately from physical component omission.
openings.prediction: With contents independently verified, an ordered-layout diagram reduces short-partition questions and unaided arrangement failures relative to the current diagram.
openings.probe: Assign the ten participants to matched five-person groups using verified sample organizers and either diagram. Record correct placement, assistance requests and completion time. Measure preparation time and replacement-diagram cost before adoption.
assumptions: Instructions replace the existing diagram within both cost caps.
Parts, footprint, capacity, removability, accepted counts and colors remain unchanged.
Five participants per condition provide exploratory evidence, not pilot success certification.

raw.assessment: The observations support investigating selection and layout interpretation together; they do not establish a common cause. Width overlap does not establish the cause of insertion retries. One hybrid is proposed as an unvalidated hypothesis.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: an order-specific removable kit sheet could serve first as a component shadow board and then as a customer placement guide. Workers place each required partition on its outline, verify count and exterior color, and pack the checked kit with the sheet. Matching temporary labels connect each outline to its destination in the ordered layout, including the short partition.
openings.delta: Adapt the relationship between tools and empty silhouettes on a tool shadow board. Failed correspondence: an organizer partition has both a packed position and an installed position, which a simple silhouette cannot equate. Change the material assumptions from a fixed reusable board to a proposed removable sheet and from workshop assembly to checked customer assembly. Cross silhouette-based inventory checking with spatial assembly guidance at the shared partition-to-slot label interface: the same checked identity survives packing and becomes a placement instruction. Neither parent alone checks both presence and intended placement.
openings.prediction: The shared mapping should reduce short-partition placement errors beyond silhouettes alone and reduce kit omissions beyond layout guidance alone. Total workshop time may fall if avoided assembly exceeds sheet preparation and checking time.
openings.probe: Use spare board for sample kits, preserving all selected counts, colors, footprint and assortment. Compare checking-only, guidance-only, combined and current workflows, recording selection, preparation, checking, insertion and packing separately. Counterbalance worker order. Give ten participants fresh kits with combined or existing guidance; record unaided placement and short-partition errors. Treat this small comparison as exploratory. Before adoption, cost sheets and labels against 500 initial and 0.40 recurring limits, include setup in delivery capacity, and test all 60 pilot orders against the stated success measures.
assumptions: Provenance: the incumbent explicitly uses an order slip and base slots; verify the slip contains enough layout information before repurposing it into a partition-to-slot mapping.
Affordable sheet production, removable labels and sufficient preparation time are enabling dependencies, not supplied resources.
Customers can assemble checked kits unaided; this remains unproven. The guide is removed before use and makes no permanent bonds.

critiques.assumption: A consistent outline-to-slot mapping also represents the accepted order correctly.
critiques.limitation: A wrong order-specific sheet could make checking and placement agree while both preserve the wrong configuration. No supplied observation establishes this failure, but internal consistency cannot independently verify the source order.
critiques.opening: Anchor sheet validation to the accepted order before letting its identities serve both stages.
critiques.comparison: The shared interface can transmit either correct identity or a common error; separate checking and guidance do not necessarily share that error source.
critiques.probe: On sample kits only, deliberately mismatch a sheet and accepted-order specification; test whether an independent source comparison detects it before packing.

critiques.assumption: Customer assembly can be changed alongside guidance without obscuring the guide's effect.
critiques.limitation: A1 changes both workshop preassembly and instructions; Z2 isolates instructions. D2-O4 already records placement difficulty, so improved guidance does not establish that transferring all assembly succeeds.
critiques.opening: Assess the shared guide while retaining preassembly, then test customer assembly separately.
critiques.comparison: This preserves A1's shared identity interaction while isolating Z2's interpretation mechanism; it initially forfeits A1's predicted assembly-time saving.
critiques.probe: Keep delivery form equal in the first customer comparison; record assembly transfer as a separate untested dependency.

openings.claim: An order-verified shared checking and placement sheet may reduce omissions and interpretation failures while retaining workshop preassembly.
openings.delta: Add an independent order-to-sheet check and separate the shared-identity mechanism from assembly transfer.
openings.prediction: Compared with checking alone, shared identities should improve placement; compared with guidance alone, they should improve content completeness. The interaction is identity continuity through packing. It fails if identities become ambiguous, parts move without correspondence, or the source mapping is wrong.
openings.probe: Use 12 samples across current, checking-only, guidance-only and combined workflows, three layouts per condition, alternating workers; time every stage including sheet validation. Compare five fresh participants per current/combined condition with equal preassembly. Verify contents independently. These proposed screens cannot establish interaction strength or pilot success; subsequently assess all stated 60-order targets.
assumptions: Sheets and removable labels are feasible within 500 initial and 0.40 recurring cost caps.
Checks and probes fit the fixed delivery date; accepted counts, colors, footprint, capacity and rearrangeability remain intact.
Retaining preassembly may leave the eight-minute target unmet.

openings.claim: Configuration switching may increase selection/checking time.
openings.discriminator: Matched layouts isolate switching from complexity and insertion.
openings.probe: Counterbalance blocked/interleaved sequences: 12 samples, six matched pairs across layouts/workers; separately time selection, insertion, checking, packing and independently count contents.
openings.uncertainty: Directional only; mixed-batch association is not causation.

openings.claim: Generic diagrams may obscure a present short partition's placement.
openings.discriminator: Verified contents isolate interpretation from omission.
openings.probe: Compare current/ordered-layout diagrams with matched five-person groups and equal preassembly; record placement, assistance, completion, preparation time and cost.
openings.uncertainty: Small exploratory comparison; reported omissions are not all physically verified.

openings.claim: Order-verified shared silhouette-to-slot identities may improve completeness and placement with preassembly retained.
openings.discriminator: Checking-only versus combined tests placement; guidance-only versus combined tests completeness; continuity may also propagate mapping errors.
openings.probe: Compare current/checking/guidance/combined using 12 samples across three layouts, alternating workers; independently verify contents and time all stages. Compare five fresh customers per current/combined condition equally preassembled. Challenge independent order checks with deliberately mismatched sample sheets.
openings.uncertainty: Mapping, label feasibility and continuity unproven; eight-minute target unresolved. Customer assembly and its time saving remain parked for separate testing.

lineage.reason: Merged with Q1; assembly-transfer distinction explicitly parked.
Merged with A1; independent source check and preassembly retained.

post_distill.decision: Exploratory synthetic hypotheses. Preserve footprint/assortment, removability, accepted counts/colors and deadline; verify initial <=500 and recurring <=0.40 costs. Screens cannot certify the 60-order completeness/time/unaided-arrangement targets.
